message.reasoning_content: Record description update. Key facts: per-row sum of 128 fp32 values; kernel sums left-to-right sequential in fp32; data has large ±w terms (up to ~33M) and small 0.25-0.75 terms; exact row sums: w + (-w) cancels exactly (integers up to 33M in fp32 exact), so reference sum = sum of 64 small values = 64*0.5ish ≈ up to 48. Sequential fp32 sum after permutation: intermediate magnitudes ~ up to 33M, small terms may be lost (0.25 vs 33M → ulp of 33M is 2, so 0.25 increments are lost when acc ~ tens of millions). Error could be up to ~ 30ish per row vs ref norm... Ref row sum ~32 avg, norm over 64 rows ~ 250; error per row up to maybe 40ish? Depends on partial sums. This is the classic cancellation trap. Risk: sequential fp32 loses small terms.
